title: Copilot Studio: share autonomous agents with end users (run-only)
summary: The roadmap facts, preview sharing behaviour, licensing and documented commands are supported. Minor corrections should include the data-policy connector's three-dot menu and acknowledge Microsoft's alternative, preview-labelled path for the embedded-credentials sharing control.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: General Availability is targeted for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Preview is targeted for August CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "August CY2026"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The record lists Web as the platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap says autonomous agents could previously only be used and managed by makers.
claims.quote: Previously, autonomous agents could only be used and managed by makers, limiting their reach to the people who needed them.

claims.claim: Run-only sharing is intended to let end users benefit without edit permissions or ownership.
claims.quote: Run-only sharing enables makers to securely share autonomous agents with end users, allowing users to benefit from agent-driven automation without requiring edit permissions or ownership.

claims.claim: A maker can share a published agent with triggers for recipients to run using their own credentials.
claims.quote: You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials.

claims.claim: The autonomous sharing panel accepts individual users and security groups.
claims.quote: Enter the user name, email addresses of individual users, or security groups you want to share the agent with. Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar.

claims.claim: Triggers and tools must be configured for user authentication before sharing.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: makers choose sharing and recipients activate it for themselves.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or environment admin switch for Can use sharing is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio run only autonomous sharing admin switch disable tenant environment; opened authoring-share-agent, admin-sharing-controls-limits, managed-environment-sharing-limits; reviewed tenant-settings and sec-gov-phase2 search excerpts. No dedicated Can use switch found.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing reflects the documented per-user licence prerequisite and consumption billing.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license. Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[6].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require recipients to have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The sharing article says users without a licence can sign up for a trial.
claims.quote: Users who don't have a license can sign up for a trial.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous usage is totalled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited pages do not state credit rates specific to autonomous run-only sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent run only credit rates per user usage reports admin instances maker disabled; opened authoring-share-agent, billing-credit-overview and manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity. No run-only-specific rate found.

claims.claim: Sharing limits are at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Environments. On the Environments page, select a managed environment. In the command bar, Edit Managed Environments. The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration with EnvironmentName and UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration saves sharing-limit settings.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.claim: The documented sharing-limit procedure retrieves governanceConfiguration with Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment.
claims.quote:
$environment = Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId>
$governanceConfiguration = $environment.Internal.properties.governanceConfiguration

claims.claim: The agent example sets extendedSettings bot-limitSharingMode and bot-maxLimitUserSharing.
claims.quote:
-Name 'bot-limitSharingMode' -Value "ExcludeSharingToSecurityGroups" -Force
-Name 'bot-maxLimitUserSharing' -Value "20" -Force

claims.claim: The agent PowerShell example prevents security-group sharing and limits viewer numbers.
claims.quote: Here's a PowerShell script that prevents agents from being shared with security groups and limits the number of viewers that can access an agent to 20.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: These sharing limits are Managed Environments controls described for Editor and Viewer assignments.
claims.quote: When you set sharing controls in the Power Platform admin center, you can enforce how makers share Editor or Viewer assignments with other individuals for their agents in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sharing-limit documentation does not explicitly establish whether Editor and Viewer rules evaluate Can use sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent "Can use" admin disable sharing approval policy; opened admin-sharing-controls-limits, managed-environment-sharing-limits and authoring-share-agent. Rules specify Editor and Viewer; no Can use mapping found.

claims.claim: The printed data-policy path reaches Microsoft Copilot Studio > Block in Assign connectors.
claims.quote: The Assign connectors page appears. Use the search box to find the connector you want. Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then: To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select Block.
claims.fix: Include the omitted unlabelled menu: Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors > Microsoft Copilot Studio > three dots > Block.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <PolicyGuid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <ConnectorObjects> assigns connectors to the Blocked policy group.
claims.quote: Adds the given connectors to the given group of the DLP policy. Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Each connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy requires id, type and name.
claims.quote: Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties: id: The unique identifier of the connector. type: The type of the connector: name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.claim: The data-policy UI procedure requires tenant admin or Environment Admin permissions.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents makers from adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: An enforced event-trigger restriction produces a detailed error in the Triggers section.
claims.quote: If the policy is enforced, a detailed error message appears in the Triggers section on the Overview page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Data policies govern connectors used by Copilot Studio agents in the policy's environments.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not specify the handling of an already-running shared autonomous instance after trigger-blocking or a policy change.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared autonomous agent running data policy changes triggers enforcement; opened admin-data-loss-prevention and reviewed admin-dlp-troubleshooting excerpts. Real-time enforcement is stated, but in-flight shared-instance handling is not.

claims.claim: For an ungrouped environment the maker credential control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: In the environment's details page, select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.claim: An API or command for Control maker credential options is not documented in the references found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "API" "PowerShell" "pac"; Copilot Studio control maker credential options Power Platform API administration powershell environment settings. Opened configure-no-maker-authentication; reviewed pac env and management SDK search results.

claims.claim: Grouped environments use Manage > Environment groups > group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: On the side navigation, select Manage. Select Environments or Environment groups. In the list that appears, select the name of the environment or environment group you want to configure.

claims.claim: This setting cannot be configured on the individual details page of a grouped environment.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.

claims.claim: Configuring the grouped-environment credential control requires a tenant admin with access to the group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: The maker credential restriction affects tools for all agents in the affected environment immediately.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: Learn warns that preventing maker credentials makes scheduled or autonomous background agents fail for missing credentials.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: Under end-user authentication, the agent cannot perform an action the user lacks permission to perform.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: The cited page places Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. Select Settings, and then select Features. Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'Microsoft also documents this control as preview under Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environments > environment > Set up, with options to let or not let makers share embedded credentials.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials.

claims.claim: No documented command or API for the embedded maker credentials sharing restriction was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "embedded maker credentials" "API" "PowerShell" "pac"; opened configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and power-platform/admin/security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials; reviewed CLI results. No operation setting this restriction found.

claims.claim: Connections configured for end-user credentials are not subject to the embedded maker connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.claim: The spending-policy procedure documents Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources > Specific environments > environment.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy. Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope. Specific environments: Choose Specific environments

claims.claim: No API for resource-based environment or per-agent spending policies was established.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph resource based spending policy Copilot Studio create API; opened cost-management/overview and the cost-management article; read spendingpolicy-create excerpts. Graph documents allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy, not resource-based scope.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A resource-based policy supports a monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A resource-based policy can also set a per-agent spending limit.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies can cover selected agents or environments.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents.

claims.claim: For covered resources, the policy moves credit management to Microsoft 365 and replaces Power Platform allocations and linked billing plans.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not apply to AI Builder features or their credits.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 spending controls take precedence over Power Platform controls for covered usage.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.claim: Until a resource-based policy is created, the existing Power Platform configuration remains in effect.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.claim: The cost-management article recommends AI Administrator for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 administrators managing spending policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies.

claims.claim: The roles page lists Global administrator or Billing administrator for creating spending policies.
claims.quote: Turn on usage-based billing and create spending policies | Microsoft 365 admin center | Global administrator or Billing administrator

claims.claim: AI administrator and License administrator can edit existing spending policies but cannot create them.
claims.quote: The AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit existing spending policies, but they can't create them.

claims.where: controls[6].ui; Governance controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: The maker selects Agents > agent > Share > Can use to assign run-only recipients.
claims.quote: Open the agent from the Agents page. Select the Share ... icon near Publish on the top menu bar. Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar. If you already shared the agent with users, change their permission to Can use.

claims.claim: No documented operation assigning autonomous Can use recipients was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agents "Can use" API Dataverse sharing permissions; "Can use" "autonomous" "Dataverse" "GrantAccess"; opened authoring-share-agent and reviewed Dataverse GrantAccess and security-role excerpts. No autonomous Can use operation established.

claims.claim: From Share, the maker selects Copy sharing link > Copy link to set up.
claims.quote: Select Copy sharing link, then Copy link to set up.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[6].note
claims.claim: Recipients receive no sharing notification, so makers must send them the setup link.
claims.quote: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them. Makers must copy and send the can use link to end users.

claims.claim: Recipients use the shared agent-management page to connect required services with their own credentials.
claims.quote: Use the agent management page to connect required services with your own credentials, configure the trigger settings that the agent owner allows, and turn triggers on or off.

claims.claim: The autonomous agent cannot run for a recipient until every required trigger, tool and workflow connection is established.
claims.quote: An autonomous agent can't run until you connect every trigger, tool, and workflow that requires your credentials.

claims.claim: Makers decide which trigger options recipients may configure using Editable by user.
claims.quote: If you're sharing this agent with others to use, choose which options users can or can't configure themselves by turning on or off Editable by user for each option.

claims.claim: Recipients cannot change instructions, tools or other authoring settings.
claims.quote: You can't change the agent's instructions, tools, or other authoring settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users of shared autonomous agents cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Tool calls are invoked and executed with AI based on the maker's specifications.
claims.quote: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.

claims.claim: A workflow used as a tool in a shared autonomous agent can accept only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.claim: Learn documents autonomous sharing as preview and its related setup behaviour as prerelease.
claims.quote:
Set up a shared autonomous agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require publication to Teams + Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to Teams + Microsoft 365, with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot to be on.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to Teams + Microsoft 365, with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: User authentication for the agent is configured to Authenticate with Microsoft.

claims.claim: Editing rights are separately assigned through environment security roles.
claims.quote: Add users to the agent's environment, and then assign users editing rights through the environment's security roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Autonomous runs can start from connected-service events without a chat prompt.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: The maker's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with trigger event details.
claims.quote: The trigger sends event details to the agent. Your agent's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with those details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Maker updates prompt users to accept changes and may require connections or consent on the management page.
claims.quote: The agent owner can update the agent, which might require you to connect or consent to the updates.

claims.claim: End users need to bookmark the management URL for health checks, fixes and consent to maker updates.
claims.quote: End users need to bookmark the agent management URL to check their agent's health, fix the agent, consent to maker updates to the agent, and other management tasks.

claims.claim: Recipients can pause and resume triggers using the Enabled toggle.
claims.quote: To pause a trigger without removing its configuration, turn the Enabled toggle off. Turn it on again when you want the trigger to run.

claims.claim: The agent management Activity tab shows recent runs and failures.
claims.quote: Use the Activity tab to review recent runs and identify failed runs.

claims.claim: No approval setting specific to run-only shared autonomous agents was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "autonomous" "approval" human review shared; opened authoring-share-agent and end-user-manage-shared-agent; read autonomous-agents guidance and AI approvals excerpts. General workflow approval design is documented, not a run-only sharing approval setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The agent-management article does not specify administrator visibility into individual recipients' instances.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous shared agent administrator instance maker account disabled; opened end-user-manage-shared-agent and authoring-share-agent. The management article describes the recipient experience, not administrative access to individual instances.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited sharing and management pages do not state what happens to recipient instances when the maker's account is disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous shared agent administrator instance maker account disabled; opened authoring-share-agent and end-user-manage-shared-agent. No maker-account-disable effect on shared recipient instances found.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not describe how shared autonomous per-user credit totals appear in reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent run only credit rates per user usage reports admin instances maker disabled; opened billing-credit-overview and capacity reporting. The latter's per-user reporting description specifies standard-harness agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness credits cover LLM tokens, tools and the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center manages Copilot Credits and permits allocation to environments.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are managed through the Power Platform admin center. Administrators can allocate credits to environments and monitor usage to ensure that sufficient credits are available.

claims.claim: The documented trigger experience builds autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Use triggers to create autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
